title_en: Guixinyuan Company v. Quanwei Company et al. — dispute over land use right transfer contract
ruling_gist_en: When entering into a contract for the transfer of state-owned land use rights, if the transferor has not obtained the state-owned land use right certificate at the time of signing the contract but has obtained it before litigation, the transfer contract shall be deemed valid. Where a party, after obtaining the state-owned land use right certificate, fails to pay the full amount of land transfer fees or fails to meet the 25% threshold of total investment for the development of the transferred land, these are defects in the subject matter of the transfer and do not affect the validity of the transfer contract.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over contract for transfer of state-owned land use rights; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region; Legal person; Contract Law; Validity of transfer contract; Failure to obtain land use right certificate; Insufficient payment of land transfer fees; Investment development less than 25%; Affirmation of original judgment; Transfer of land use rights; Land transfer fees not fully paid; Contract dispute; Land use rights; Etc. dispute over transfer of land use rights contract
full_text_en:
Guixin Yuan Company v. Quanwei Company et al. — Dispute over Land Use Rights Transfer Contract

【Ruling Summary】

When concluding a contract for the transfer of state-owned land use rights, if the transferor has not yet obtained the state-owned land use rights certificate at the time of contracting but obtains it before the lawsuit, the transfer contract shall be deemed valid. If the party, after obtaining the state-owned land use rights certificate, fails to pay the full amount of the land grant fee, or if its investment and development in the transferred land do not reach 25% or more of the total investment, these are defects in the subject matter of the transfer and do not affect the validity of the transfer contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 46

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Liuzhou Quanwei Electrical Appliance Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 153 Liushi Road, Liuzhou City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Liu Quanzhang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Tian Kuang, attorney at Beijing Jiahe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Luo Maolong, attorney at Beijing Jiahe Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Liuzhou Chaofan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 29 Changqing Road, Chengzhong District, Liuzhou City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Qin Jinsheng, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Luo Maolong, attorney at Beijing Jiahe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Tian Kuang, attorney at Beijing Jiahe Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Nanning Guixinyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 48 Shenyang Road, Nanning City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Luo Xianyou, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Zhengguo, attorney at Sichuan Kangwei Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Huang Yuan, attorney at Sichuan Kangwei Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over a land use rights transfer contract between appellants Liuzhou Quanwei Electrical Appliance Co., Ltd. and Liuzhou Chaofan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and appellee Nanning Guixinyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd., the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region rendered a civil judgment (2004) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 1 on April 18, 2004. Liuzhou Quanwei Electrical Appliance Co., Ltd. and Liuzhou Chaofan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing on July 15, 2004. Tian Kuang and Luo Maolong, agents ad litem for Liuzhou Quanwei Electrical Appliance Co., Ltd. and Liuzhou Chaofan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Luo Xianyou, legal representative of Nanning Guixinyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd., and Li Zhengguo, his agent ad litem, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial the following facts:

On September 18, 2003, Liuzhou Quanwei Electrical Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Quanwei Company), Liuzhou Chaofan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chaofan Company), and Nanning Guixinyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guixinyuan Company) entered into a "Land Development Contract" stipulating that Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company agreed to transfer to Guixinyuan Company a parcel of land of 51.9979 mu located at No. 153 Liushi Road, Liuzhou City, owned by Quanwei Company, with a transfer price of RMB 28.6 million. In view of the fact that Chaofan Company had invested preliminary funds and done some preliminary work after entering into the "Agreement" on March 31, 2003 with Quanwei Company, after this agreement was signed, Quanwei Company agreed that Guixinyuan Company pay Chaofan Company compensation of RMB 16.4 million. The payment schedule and method for the land transfer price: According to Quanwei Company's requirements, Guixinyuan Company agreed to transfer RMB 2 million into Quanwei Company's account as a cooperation deposit before September 30, 2003; if overdue, Guixinyuan Company would be deemed in default, and Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company would have the right to unilaterally terminate the contract. Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company must, within two months, complete the procedures to obtain the municipal government's consent for the transfer of the land to a newly established company in Liuzhou controlled by Guixinyuan Company or by the legal representative of Guixinyuan Company, and grant land development plan quotas for this year or the first half of the next year. Within one month from the date Guixinyuan Company obtains approval of the development quota and can commence real estate development, it shall, on behalf of Quanwei Company, pay the loan of RMB 7.95 million owed to the Liuzhou Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and the interest within the balance sheet of RMB 960,000 (if such interest can be reduced or waived, this amount shall be added to the factory relocation fee). If this loan can be transferred to Guixinyuan Company with the bank's consent, Quanwei Company shall actively assist Guixinyuan Company in handling the procedures and provide the land as collateral for the loan. If, due to the transfer of the loan to Guixinyuan Company, the interest within the balance sheet of RMB 960,000 (the exact amount subject to bank confirmation) cannot be waived, Guixinyuan Company shall bear such interest; for any other reason, if Quanwei Company does not obtain interest waiver from the bank, Quanwei Company shall bear the cost. Within one month from the date Guixinyuan Company obtains municipal government approval for the transfer of the land to the newly established company in Liuzhou controlled by Guixinyuan Company or by its legal representative and obtains the development quota approval to commence real estate development, it must, on behalf of Quanwei Company, pay the land use nature change fee (from industrial to commercial) and deed tax of approximately RMB 6 million to the land administration department. Within three months from the date Quanwei Company completes the transfer of the land to the Liuzhou company controlled by Guixinyuan Company or by its legal representative, the Liuzhou company controlled by Guixinyuan Company or by its legal representative shall, on behalf of Quanwei Company, pay in installments the employee resettlement fee, factory relocation fee, and repay Quanwei Company's miscellaneous small debts, totaling approximately RMB 6 million. The above total of RMB 23 million shall be deducted from the land transfer price payable by Guixinyuan Company to Quanwei Company; the remaining RMB 22 million (Guixinyuan Company, according to the requirements of Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company, pays RMB 5.6 million to Quanwei Company and RMB 16.4 million to Chaofan Company) shall be paid by Guixinyuan Company to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company within one year from the date Guixinyuan Company obtains land use and development quota approval and can commence real estate development. If, due to reasons of the government and real estate development and construction management departments (including overall planning, municipal construction, and municipal management), or due to reasons of Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company (including reasons of Quanwei Company's employees, surrounding units and individuals), or due to debt collection by creditors of Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company, and other reasons not attributable to Guixinyuan Company, the procedures for project construction commencement cannot be completed within six months and construction cannot start, the payment period shall be correspondingly extended according to the actual duration of the delay. If Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company wish to purchase commercial housing developed by Guixinyuan Company on the said land, the purchase price may be deducted from the fees payable by Guixinyuan Company to Quanwei Company. At the same time as Guixinyuan Company pays the land nature change fee and deed tax to the Land Bureau on behalf of Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company, Quanwei Company must transfer the land to the newly established company in Liuzhou controlled by Guixinyuan Company or by its legal representative. However, before Guixinyuan Company pays Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company the full RMB 45 million, it shall not transfer the land to any person other than the company controlled by Guixinyuan Company or by its legal representative. The term of the land use rights transferred by Quanwei Company to Guixinyuan Company shall be handled in accordance with the relevant government regulations. Guixinyuan Company plans to develop the land in phases. From the date Guixinyuan Company pays the factory relocation fee and employee resettlement fee for the portion of land to be developed, Quanwei Company must complete the relocation within three and a half months, remove all debris, and deliver the land to Guixinyuan Company with three connections and one leveling (water, electricity, road connections and land leveling). For the portion of the price not yet paid by Guixinyuan Company to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company, Guixinyuan Company or its Liuzhou controlled company or the company controlled by its legal representative shall provide land and real estate of corresponding value as mortgage guarantee. If Quanwei Company or Chaofan Company, due to their own reasons, fail to complete the land transfer procedures, change of land use nature, and land development quota processing within the time limits stipulated in the contract, or fail to complete the removal of all attachments on the land and achieve three connections and one leveling on time, they shall pay penalty interest to Guixinyuan Company at a rate of one-thousandth of the amount already paid by Guixinyuan Company per day of delay. If the delay exceeds 30 days, Guixinyuan Company has the right to unilaterally terminate the contract. If Guixinyuan Company proposes termination of the contract for the above reasons, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company shall double refund the RMB 2 million deposit. If Guixinyuan Company fails to pay in full the relevant amounts to the relevant units on behalf of Quanwei Company within the time limits stipulated in the contract, or fails to pay Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company the full land transfer price and compensation, Guixinyuan Company shall pay penalty interest to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company respectively at a rate of one-thousandth of the amount payable per day of delay. If the delay exceeds 30 days, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company have the right to unilaterally terminate the contract. If Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company unilaterally propose termination of the contract for the above reasons, the RMB 2 million deposit paid by Guixinyuan Company shall be treated as compensation for breach of contract to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company. It was also agreed that this contract is a tripartite execution contract, and the "Agreement" signed on March 31, 2003 between Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company and the "Real Estate Project Cooperative Development Contract" signed on September 1, 2003 between Quanwei Company and Guixinyuan Company shall be simultaneously voided upon the signing of this contract. On September 29, 2003, Guixinyuan Company transferred the RMB 2 million deposit into Quanwei Company's account. On November 18, 2003, the Liuzhou Municipal Development and Reform Commission approved the change of use of the land involved in this case to commercial use. On November 3, 2003, Guixinyuan Company sent a letter to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company, authorizing Liuzhou Shengyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd., controlled by Guixinyuan Company's legal representative Luo Xianyou, to perform the contract on its behalf, and requesting Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company to transfer the land to Liuzhou Shengyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd. in accordance with the contract. On December 15, 2003, Guixinyuan Company again sent a letter to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company, changing the performing company to Liuzhou Hengmaoyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd., and requesting Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company to transfer the land to that company in accordance with the contract. On November 21, 2003, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company sent a letter to Guixinyuan Company, stating that on November 18, 2003, they had completed the document approving the change of land use from the Liuzhou Municipal Development and Reform Commission, and a copy had been provided to Guixinyuan Company. They requested Guixinyuan Company to pay RMB 6 million in advance, of which RMB 3 million would be used to pay land use fees, handle land transfer and release of liens, and factory relocation; the other RMB 3 million would be paid within one month after completion of land transfer procedures. On November 25, 2003, Quanwei Company proposed a fund plan: The first phase fund plan totaled RMB 3 million, including: 1. Payment of RMB 420,000 owed to Hebei Technology Co., Ltd. to handle land lien release; 2. Payment of land use fee of RMB 1.2 million; 3. Factory relocation costs of RMB 1 million; 4. Repayment of other miscellaneous small debts of RMB 380,000. The second phase fund should be in place within one month after land transfer. On December 2, 2003, Chaofan Company and Quanwei Company again sent a letter to Guixinyuan Company: First, according to the results obtained by Chaofan Company and Quanwei Company from the principal responsible persons of the Liuzhou Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, if the principal of the bank debt is repaid within this year, all interest within and outside the balance sheet will be waived; the policy for next year is not yet clear. Therefore, Guixinyuan Company is requested to repay the bank debt in full this year on behalf of Liuzhou Magnetic Motor Factory (i.e., Quanwei Company) in accordance with the contract. If the method of debt assumption is adopted, Guixinyuan Company must undertake to bear all interest. Second, Guixinyuan Company must promptly confirm in writing the final cooperating company and provide copies of legal certifications of that company. Third, Guixinyuan Company must provide the mortgage guarantee procedures stipulated in the contract, so that both parties can proceed to the next step of land processing. In this letter, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company also stated that they had sent a letter to Guixinyuan Company on November 21, 2003, but had not received a reply. To demonstrate sincerity in cooperation, they are again sending a letter, hoping Guixinyuan Company will reply within five days so that the operational procedures of cooperation can proceed; otherwise, all consequences and full responsibility shall be borne by Guixinyuan Company. On December 18, 2003, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company sent a letter to Guixinyuan Company: Because Article 7 of the "Land Development Contract" did not clearly stipulate the time, collateral, guarantee scope, and guarantee amount for the mortgage guarantee to be provided by Guixinyuan Company, the three parties considered it necessary to amend and perfect this clause and discussed this issue at meetings on November 5, December 15, and December 16, 2003, but no agreement was reached. On November 22 and December 2, 2003, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company had also sent letters to Guixinyuan Company twice, requesting Guixinyuan Company to provide mortgage procedures, but Guixinyuan Company has not yet replied. Whether Guixinyuan Company can provide and complete mortgage guarantee registration procedures is crucial to ensuring the future realization of the interests of Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company. Therefore, they are again sending a letter, hoping that Guixinyuan Company will come to Quanwei Company by December 8, 2003, to discuss the revision and improvement of the above issues and ultimately reach an agreement; otherwise, the "Land Development Contract" cannot be performed, and the three parties will completely terminate the contract. On December 20, 2003, Liuzhou Hengmaoyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd. replied to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company: The "Land Development Contract" fully reflects the will of the three parties and is fair and lawful; a breaching party cannot arbitrarily terminate the contract without the other party's breach or agreement to termination. Our company expressed at the consultation meetings on November 15 and 16 and at the meeting on November 19 that we will firmly execute whatever is stipulated in the contract, and that transferring the land to our company is safe and without risk. Now, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company, citing non-existent risk factors, refuse to handle the land transfer, which constitutes a serious breach. Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company should demonstrate their sincerity in cooperation through concrete actions; only after the contract is actually performed can the three parties negotiate matters beyond the contract. On December 29, 2003, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company sent a letter to Guixinyuan Company, stating that the three parties had failed to reach an agreement on the time, guarantee amount, and guarantee scope for mortgage guarantee registration, and Guixinyuan Company was unwilling to negotiate; moreover, Quanwei Company is a restructured enterprise, and whether Guixinyuan Company can provide effective mortgage guarantee concerns the future livelihood of employees and social stability. Therefore, they decided to terminate the "Land Development Contract" effective from that date and requested Guixinyuan Company to discuss the return of the deposit. On January 3, 2004, Guixinyuan Company sent a letter to Chaofan Company and Quanwei Company, refusing to terminate the contract.

The court of first instance additionally found that on January 18, 2004, the Yufeng Sub-Branch of the Liuzhou Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China replied to Liuzhou Hengmaoyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd.: 1. As long as the principal of the loan owed to our bank is repaid in full, our bank will release the mortgage on the said land use rights in accordance with regulations; 2. Based on the above principle, if your company repays the full amount of principal and interest owed by the debtor Liuzhou Magnetic Motor Factory to our bank, our bank will release the mortgage on the said land use rights.

The court of first instance also found that Quanwei Company was established through the restructuring of Liuzhou Magnetic Motor Factory in 2003, and its business license shows a business period from June 8, 2003. The land involved in this case, located at No. 153 Liushi Road, Liuzhou City, is state-owned granted land, with land certificate No. Liu Guo Yong (2003) Zi No. 188461, land area of 34,665.3 square meters (approximately 51.9979 mu), and use as industrial land. Quanwei Company acquired the land through a "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed with the Liuzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources on June 26, 2003. The land was subject to a mortgage registration under a mortgage contract, with a mortgaged area of 34,537.3 square meters and a mortgage amount of RMB 8.37 million, with a mortgage period from July 11, 1997 to July 9, 1999. The mortgagee is the Liuzhou Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China. The mortgage has expired but has not yet been deregistered. Quanwei Company, after its corporate restructuring, disposed of the land use rights by way of grant and still owes RMB 2.925 million in employee economic compensation, which has not been paid. On November 18, 2003, the Liuzhou Municipal Development and Reform Commission notified Quanwei Company: The 9th working meeting of the Liuzhou Municipal Land Acquisition, Reserve and Approval Committee in 2003 has approved the change of use of the land at No. 153 Liushi Road to commercial use. Please go through the relevant procedures with the Municipal Development and Reform Commission, Planning Bureau, Land Bureau, and other relevant departments from the date of this notice until June 30, 2004; failure to do so within the period will be deemed automatic abandonment. The notice also stated: 1. If a real estate development company changes the use of its land, please go through the procedures according to the relevant procedures for real estate development projects; 2. If a non-real estate development company changes the use of its land, it must first obtain real estate development qualifications and then go through the procedures according to the relevant procedures for real estate development projects.

On January 13, 2004, Guixinyuan Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging that it, Quanwei Company, and Chaofan Company had entered into the "Land Development Contract" on September 18, 2003, stipulating that Guixinyuan Company would acquire 51.9979 mu of land owned by Quanwei Company at No. 153 Liushi Road, Liuzhou City, for real estate development at a price of RMB 28.6 million. Guixinyuan Company would pay a deposit of RMB 2 million to Quanwei Company before September 30, 2003, and the contract would take effect. After the contract was signed, Guixinyuan Company paid the deposit of RMB 2 million on time. According to the contract, Quanwei Company must, within two months from the effective date of the contract, complete the procedures to transfer the land to a newly established company in Liuzhou controlled by Guixinyuan Company or by its legal representative, and grant land development plan quotas for this year or the first half of the next year. However, Quanwei Company has been overdue for 40 days and still does not apply to the land administration department for the transfer procedures, and on December 29, 2003, it sent a letter to Guixinyuan Company terminating the "Land Development Contract," rendering the contract unenforceable and causing huge losses to Guixinyuan Company. Therefore, Guixinyuan Company requests: 1. A ruling that the "Land Development Contract" signed on September 18, 2003, is valid and that Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company should continue to perform it. 2. That Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company double refund the deposit of RMB 4 million and compensate for all economic losses caused to Guixinyuan Company. 3. That Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company bear all litigation costs of this case.

Quanwei Company argued in defense: First, it did not agree to continue performing the contract. Quanwei Company was an enterprise in extreme difficulty. After obtaining the development quota, it requested Guixinyuan Company to provide mortgage guarantee for the unpaid amount. Guixinyuan Company rejected this legitimate request. Therefore, Quanwei Company had lost trust in Guixinyuan Company, and if performance continued, Quanwei Company would bear significant risk. Second, it did not agree to double refund of the deposit. Quanwei Company had no breach of contract in this case; it terminated the cooperation with Guixinyuan Company lawfully. Third, it did not agree to compensate Guixinyuan Company for economic losses. Guixinyuan Company had no specific claim for damages, and the precondition for compensation was that Quanwei Company was in breach.

Chaofan Company argued in defense: First, at the time of the signing of the Land Development Contract on September 18, 2003, Quanwei Company did not possess independent civil subject qualification; the contract should be invalid. Moreover, Chaofan Company requested Guixinyuan Company to provide guarantee for the payables of over RMB 10,000,000, but Guixinyuan Company refused to provide it, so Chaofan Company bore significant risk. Therefore, Chaofan Company did not agree to continue performing the contract. Second, Chaofan Company did not receive the deposit of RMB 2,000,000 and had no breach, thus it did not agree to double refund of the deposit. Third, it did not agree to compensate Guixinyuan Company for economic losses. Guixinyuan Company had no specific amount of loss, and Chaofan Company was not in breach in this case. The deposit penalty rule and the liquidated damages rule cannot be applied simultaneously; claiming double refund of the deposit precludes claiming damages.

The court of first instance held after trial that the nature of this case is a dispute over a contract for the transfer of land use rights. The Land Development Contract signed by the three parties was based on voluntary and mutual agreement. The subject matter of the transfer under the contract was land that Quanwei Company had obtained through grant and had the right to use, and which had been approved by relevant authorities for real estate development; this land could enter the market, and the contract's contents did not violate legal provisions. As to the issue raised by Chaofan Company that Quanwei Company had exceeded its term of operation at the time of contract signing, according to the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, the civil capacity of a legal person starts from its establishment and ends with its termination. In this case, Quanwei Company did not terminate upon the expiration of its business term; its business license had not been cancelled or revoked, and as a corporate legal person, it still lawfully exists and its legal personality has not terminated. Moreover, the contract in this case was not within the scope of business specified in its business license but was a voluntary disposition of its own property, consistent with the legitimate principle of autonomy of will. Therefore, the contract in this case is valid. Chaofan Company's claim that the contract is invalid has no legal or factual basis and is not supported. For a valid contract, in accordance with the principle of good faith, all parties must abide by the contract and perform it fully. Guixinyuan Company had performed the contract by paying the deposit and informing Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company of the company that would perform on its behalf as agreed in the contract. However, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company failed to perform their own obligations as agreed in the contract. Instead, on the grounds that the mortgage guarantee clause in the contract was unclear, that no consensus was reached, and that their interests were at risk, they refused to handle the relevant land procedures as agreed and further demanded termination of the contract, which is clearly contrary to the contract. According to the contract, after Guixinyuan Company transferred the deposit of RMB 2,000,000 to Quanwei Company's account, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company were obligated to perform the obligations set out in Article 3, paragraph 2 of the contract. There was no issue of Guixinyuan Company having to first handle mortgage procedures, because the contract did not make Guixinyuan Company's handling of mortgage procedures a precondition for Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company to perform that obligation. Moreover, upon overall analysis of the contract, the "partial amount not paid by Guixinyuan Company to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company" referred to in Article 7 of the contract does not refer to the remaining amount payable after the RMB 2,000,000 deposit, but rather to the remaining RMB 22,000,000 after payment of RMB 23,000,000 as referred to in Article 3, paragraph 3 of the contract. Only at that time and during the transfer procedures would there be risk, making it necessary to require Guixinyuan Company to provide mortgage guarantee for the unpaid balance. Thus, the mortgage guarantee clause in the contract is not unclear. Furthermore, even if the mortgage guarantee clause were unclear as claimed by Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company, this would not affect the performance of the contract. According to the contract, in performing the contract in this case, Guixinyuan Company, in addition to paying the deposit of RMB 2,000,000 to Quanwei Company, had to perform related obligations on behalf of Quanwei Company and pay approximately RMB 15,000,000 before it could actually obtain the land transfer. Guixinyuan Company also promised to use the transferred land use right as mortgage guarantee for the unpaid amount; this promise does not violate legal provisions and is feasible. Therefore, the risk claimed by Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company has no factual basis, does not exist, and is not supported. In summary, the actions of Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company in this case have constituted a breach of contract, and they must bear liability for breach; they are not entitled to claim termination of the contract. Guixinyuan Company, as the compliant party, has a legally founded claim for continued performance of the contract, which is upheld. Guixinyuan Company's claim for compensation for all losses is not supported and is dismissed because no specific amount of loss or corresponding evidence was provided. Since Guixinyuan Company's claim for continued performance of the contract has been upheld by this court, its claim for double refund of the RMB 2,000,000 deposit by Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company is not only inconsistent with the agreement of the three parties in the contract but also falls outside the scope of application of the deposit penalty rule. The double refund under that rule applies only when performance fails to materialize. Therefore, Guixinyuan Company's claim in this regard is also unfounded and is not supported. Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 8, 60, and 107 of the Contract Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), the judgment is as follows: 1. Guixinyuan Company, Quanwei Company, and Chaofan Company shall continue to perform the Land Development Contract signed by the three parties on September 18, 2003, and Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company shall, within five working days from the date this judgment takes effect, complete the relevant procedures for the transfer of land in accordance with Article 3, paragraph 2 of the contract; 2. Guixinyuan Company's other claims are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 179,010 is to be borne by Guixinyuan Company in the amount of RMB 35,802, by Chaofan Company in the amount of RMB 71,604, and by Quanwei Company in the amount of RMB 71,604. The property preservation fee of RMB 143,629 is to be borne by Chaofan Company and Quanwei Company.

Quanwei Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, requesting that the judgment be amended according to law, that Guixinyuan Company's claims be dismissed, and that the contract be rescinded, with Guixinyuan Company bearing liability for breach. Main reasons: 1. The first instance judgment erred in its determination of the mortgage guarantee clause. The disputed land is the subject matter of the land transfer, not the subject matter of mortgage, and only Quanwei Company has the right to create a mortgage on that land. Guixinyuan Company's claim that Quanwei Company should transfer all land use rights to it and then use the land as collateral to provide guarantee to Quanwei Company is unreasonable. 2. The "partial amount" stipulated in Article 7 of the contract should refer to all unpaid amounts, and Quanwei Company has the right to require Guixinyuan Company to perform the guarantee obligation at any time as needed for contract performance. The first instance judgment confused actual breach with anticipatory breach, which is manifestly unfair. 3. The timing of land transfer and provision of mortgage guarantee should be determined on the basis of simultaneous performance. Under the circumstances that Guixinyuan Company failed to provide land and real estate of corresponding value as mortgage guarantee as agreed, the parties could not reach a consensus, and Guixinyuan Company lacked the capacity to perform, Quanwei Company's proposal to rescind the contract was in accordance with law. The first instance judgment's finding that Quanwei Company's demand that Guixinyuan Company perform the guarantee obligation constituted a breach was erroneous. 4. Article 3, paragraph 2 of the Land Development Contract mainly stipulated Guixinyuan Company's payment obligation, i.e., the prerequisite for Quanwei Company to transfer the land to Guixinyuan Company; it did not stipulate an obligation for Quanwei Company to transfer the land to Guixinyuan Company. After both parties received the land development quota from the Liuzhou Municipal Development and Planning Commission on November 18, 2003, Quanwei Company had already fulfilled the obligations under Article 3, paragraph 2. Guixinyuan Company should have paid the principal and interest of RMB 8,910,000 to the Liuzhou Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China within one month, i.e., before December 18, 2003. However, Guixinyuan Company only paid the deposit of RMB 2,000,000 and did not pay the remaining amounts. Meanwhile, Article 4 of the Land Development Contract stipulated that the time for Quanwei Company to transfer the land to the new company established by Guixinyuan Company should be when Guixinyuan Company pays the land use change fee and deed tax of RMB 6,000,000, i.e., the conditions for Quanwei Company's obligation to transfer the land had not yet been fulfilled. Therefore, the cause of the dispute was Guixinyuan Company's failure to perform the contract on time and its express indication that it would not perform the principal obligation of providing guarantee. The first instance judgment's determination that Guixinyuan Company was the "compliant party" was erroneous. 5. The first instance judgment required Quanwei Company to perform the land transfer obligation unilaterally within "five working days" without requiring Guixinyuan Company to assume corresponding obligations, which is inconsistent with the contract. Moreover, the first instance judgment exceeded the content of the tripartite contract and required Chaofan Company, which is not the holder of the land use right, to perform an obligation it could not fulfill, which has no legal basis.

Chaofan Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, requesting confirmation that the Land Development Contract is invalid and that both parties bear equal fault liability. Main reasons: 1. The contract for transfer of land use rights in this case violated the mandatory provisions of laws and regulations and should be held invalid. Among other things, the state-owned land grant fee has not been fully paid; there is still an outstanding amount of RMB 2,925,000 for workers' economic compensation and over RMB 970,000 for land proceeds; the parties have not invested any development funds in the "industrial land" and have not even reached the 25% investment threshold; at the time of contract signing, the state-owned land use right certificate had not been obtained; before and after the contract was signed, the disputed land was under seizure by relevant courts; the transfer of the disputed land was not notified to the mortgagee, the Liuzhou Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China; the transfer of the "industrial land" in question did not go through the corresponding approval and registration procedures. 2. Guixinyuan Company, as an enterprise specialized in real estate development, knew of the existence of the above circumstances rendering the contract invalid and the relevant laws and regulations, so both parties should bear equal fault for the invalidity of the contract.

Guixinyuan Company responded that the first instance judgment had clear factual findings and correct application of law, and should be upheld. Main reasons: 1. The contract for transfer of land use rights in this case complies with the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Urban Real Estate Administration Law) and the Contract Law, and should be held valid. Quanwei Company had paid the land grant fee of RMB 800,805 in a lump sum after the grant contract was signed; its outstanding workers' economic compensation and land proceeds are not part of the land grant fee. Quanwei Company obtained the land use right certificate before the lawsuit was filed, has the right to dispose of the land involved, and meets the statutory conditions for transfer. The land involved is industrial land, and the grant contract contains no agreement on investment development or construction of buildings on the land, so the 25% investment requirement under the Urban Real Estate Administration Law does not apply to the transfer of land use rights in this case. The mortgagee was not only aware of the land transfer but also explicitly consented to it. 2. Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company refused to perform their contractual obligations, constituting a serious breach. Their appellate arguments that Guixinyuan Company breached and should have the contract rescinded are untenable. After the contract took effect, Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company not only failed to transfer the land use rights to the company designated by Guixinyuan Company but also did not even initiate the application procedures for the transfer, which is a serious violation of the contract. The claims by Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company that Guixinyuan Company must first provide mortgage guarantee before the land transfer procedures could begin, and that Guixinyuan Company must provide mortgage guarantee for the entire transfer payment, have no contractual basis. There is no issue of unclear contract terms or other risks in this case. Article 3, paragraph 2 of the contract is the only provision in the contract regarding the obligation of Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company to handle the transfer of land use rights, i.e., the condition for Guixinyuan Company to pay the transfer price other than the deposit of RMB 2,000,000 is that Quanwei Company first transfers the land use rights to the company designated by Guixinyuan Company, after Guixinyuan Company receives approval of the development quota and can proceed with real estate development. In this case, the conditions for Guixinyuan Company to pay the transfer price have not yet been satisfied, and there is no issue of breach. The claim by Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company that Guixinyuan Company failed to pay the transfer price as agreed and that the contract should be rescinded is untenable.

This Court found on second instance that on December 17, 2003, after the Liuzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and Quanwei Company signed the State-Owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract, Quanwei Company obtained the state-owned land use right certificate for the land at No. 153, Liushi Road, Liuzhou. Other facts found by this Court on appeal are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

This Court holds that the Land Development Contract signed by Quanwei Company, Chaofan Company, and Guixinyuan Company on September 18, 2003 provided that Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company would transfer the land use rights of the land at No. 153, Liushi Road, Liuzhou to Guixinyuan Company, and Guixinyuan Company would pay RMB 28,600,000 to Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company as the land transfer price. Therefore, the nature of this case is a dispute over a contract for the transfer of land use rights. The Land Development Contract was a true expression of intent reached after consultation among the three parties, and its contents do not violate legal provisions. Before the contract was signed, the Liuzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources had already agreed that Quanwei Company would obtain the use right of the disputed land by grant, and the two parties had signed the State-Owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract. Before the initiation of the lawsuit at first instance, Quanwei Company had obtained the state-owned land use right certificate, and the disputed land had the conditions to enter the market for lawful transfer. The issue of payment of the land grant fee pertains to the rights and obligations between the parties to the land grant contract, i.e., the Liuzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and Quanwei Company, and whether such payment has been fully performed does not affect the determination of the validity of the land use rights transfer contract in this case. Therefore, this Court does not support Chaofan Company's appellate argument that the Land Development Contract should be held invalid because the state-owned land use right certificate had not been obtained at the time of signing and the land grant fee had not been fully paid, in violation of mandatory legal provisions. Regarding the issue of investment development, Article 38 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law, which provides that investment must reach 25% of the total development investment at the time of land transfer, imposes a restrictive condition on the subject matter of the contract for transfer of land use rights at the time of real rights change. If the transferred land has not reached 25% investment, this constitutes a defect in the subject matter of the contract and does not directly affect the validity of the contract for transfer of land use rights. This provision in Article 38 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law is not a mandatory legal provision for determining the validity of a land use rights transfer contract. Therefore, this Court also does not support Chaofan Company's argument that the Land Development Contract should be held invalid for failing to meet the 25% investment development condition. Regarding the issue of whether the transfer of land use rights had been notified to the mortgagee, the evidence, including the reply letter from the Liuzhou Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China to Liuzhou Hengmaoyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd. dated January 18, 2004, the letters of December 2, 2003 from Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company to the Liuzhou Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China concerning the settlement of bank loans, and the provisions of Article 3, paragraph 2 of the Land Development Contract regarding the amount and handling of mortgage debt by the three parties, all indicate that the mortgagee of the disputed land, the Liuzhou Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, knew of the transfer of the land use rights and did not object. Chaofan Company's argument that the transfer is invalid due to failure to notify the land mortgagee is inconsistent with the facts and cannot stand. In summary, although the Land Development Contract had certain defects at the time of signing, after correction, there are no circumstances violating mandatory legal provisions, and the contract should be held valid. The determination of the validity of the contract by the court of first instance applied the law correctly and should be upheld. Where the parties in the performance of a valid contract have differing interpretations of the contract clauses, the true meaning of the disputed clause shall be determined by the methods of contract interpretation provided in the Contract Law. The first instance judgment, based on the purpose of the contract and the relationship between clauses, confirmed that the "unpaid amount" under Article 7 of the Land Development Contract for which Guixinyuan Company should provide mortgage guarantee refers to the remaining RMB 22,000,000 after Guixinyuan Company pays RMB 23,000,000 on behalf of Quanwei Company in accordance with Article 3 of the contract. This factual determination is not improper. Quanwei Company's requirement that Guixinyuan Company first provide mortgage guarantee for the entire transfer price as a precondition for performing its contractual obligations is inconsistent with the contract. Furthermore, since Liuzhou Hengmaoyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd. is not the debtor for payment obligations under the Land Development Contract, the issue of its registered capital is not relevant to determining whether Guixinyuan Company has the capacity to perform. Therefore, where Quanwei Company failed to provide precise evidence that Guixinyuan Company would not perform or could not perform the contract when the performance period arrived, the conditions for Quanwei Company to exercise the right to rescind the contract had not yet been met. Accordingly, Quanwei Company's claim to rescind the contract on the grounds of performance risk lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported by this Court. Regarding the issue of handling land transfer procedures, although the Land Development Contract contains inaccuracies in the drafting of successive clauses, a comprehensive assessment of the textual expressions, transaction practices, and other factors leads to the determination that the provision in Article 3, paragraph 2 regarding "completing the procedures for the municipal government's consent to the transfer of the land to a newly established company in Liuzhou controlled by Guixinyuan Company or controlled by the legal representative of Guixinyuan Company, and granting the land development plan quota for this year or the first half of next year" refers to the obligation of Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company to handle the procedures for the government's consent to the transfer of land use rights to the company designated in the contract and for the government to grant the land development quota. Article 4 of the contract should then be Quanwei Company's obligation to handle the procedures for the change of land use rights transfer with the land administration authority. Quanwei Company's claim that the land use change procedures it had already handled with the approval of the Liuzhou Municipal Development and Planning Commission constituted performance of the obligation under Article 3, paragraph 2 is inconsistent with the contract terms. The first instance judgment's finding that Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company failed to perform the obligations under Article 3, paragraph 2 of the contract on time after Guixinyuan Company paid the deposit, constituting a breach, is not improper in its application of law. As for the time limit for Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company to perform their obligations under Article 3, paragraph 2 of the Land Development Contract, the first instance judgment specified five working days, which is consistent with the actual circumstances of this case. In conclusion, the first instance judgment had clear factual findings and correct application of law. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance, RMB 179,010, shall be borne equally by Quanwei Company and Chaofan Company.

This judgment is final.
